Non-sync mode uses salesforceTokenSchema which includes instance_url, so corruption only in sync mode — matching the finding. The mechanism is verifiable from the diff.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the refresh flow parses the token response via `parseRefreshTokenResponse(accessTokenJson, salesforceTokenSchema)` and then persists `key: { ...accessTokenParsed.data, refresh_token: credentialKey.refresh_token }` (full replacement of the credential key object). In `parseRefreshTokenResponse`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` it intentionally validates against a minimal schema (access_token + numeric expiry) rather than the full app schema. That means in sync mode the parsed `data` can omit Salesforce-required fields like `instance_url`, `id`, `issued_at`, `signature` defined in `salesforceTokenSchema`, and this update would drop them from the stored credential key, effectively corrupting the Salesforce credential for later use.
